scope.outerFoldAssignments: Frozen from experiments/diagnostics/behavior/preregister-perea-nested-animal-evaluation-2026-10.json; same 5,582 rows as existing nested evaluation.
scope.primaryMetric: equal-animal mean of per-animal F1 for RE and RU; every animal has equal weight
scope.developmentCaveat: This rule family and persistence smoother were designed after inspection of the frozen Perea baseline. Nested OOF is development evidence only, not a new independent validation or an external-ranch result.
scope.thresholdInterpretation: Two fixed-domain cutpoints: current MI level and absolute one-minute MI change. This gives four MI quadrants; a one-feature ordinal rule with only two cutpoints cannot represent four ordered behavior labels.

preprocessing.thresholdsChosenUsing: Stitched inner OOF predictions from five animal-group folds inside each outer training set; outer labels never enter threshold selection.

persistence.base: The two-threshold MI rule, with its own threshold pair selected in inner grouped OOF.
persistence.transitionRule: Switch from the prior predicted label after 2 consecutive differing instantaneous rule predictions; output prior prediction before confirmation.
persistence.seed: Instantaneous rule prediction at each contiguous animal-window start.
persistence.reset: Animal change or any timestamp difference other than exactly one minute resets to the instantaneous prediction and clears pending state.

preprocessing.deduplication: Reuses the frozen same-label collapse/conflict-exclusion policy; no refitting of earlier baseline models.

frozenReference.comparisonGuardrail: The reference nested selection was itself development on this source. It is not an independent benchmark; report alongside this diagnostic only as context.

limitations: Only 24 animal groups and two ranches; the outer folds do not establish independent site transfer.
The thresholds and persistence design were made after the frozen baseline was inspected; this nested run is development-only.
One scalar MI compresses axes and head/jaw movement; RE and RU remain difficult to separate.
Minute records are autocorrelated and source annotations carry short behaviors forward; rows are not independent replicates.
These behavior labels do not validate DMI, ADG, intake, BR-CORTE, or the Riose engine.
